dedupe_keys.name: global 3d rocket launch and re entry emissions inventory for the megaconstellation era 2020 2022

description: This inventory gives global, hourly, three-dimensional emissions of air pollutants and carbon dioxide from rocket launches and object re-entries for 2020 to 2022, the onset of the satellite megaconstellation era. It combines launch activity from the ESA DISCOSweb database and re-entries from the General Catalog of Artificial Space Objects, cross-checked against launch vehicle manuals and mission guides, with altitude-dependent emission indices that account for afterburning. Launch byproducts are CO2, water vapour, black carbon, alumina, HCl, chlorine and CO, and re-entry byproducts are NOx and alumina, split into megaconstellation and other missions. Emissions are gridded at 4 x 5 and 2 x 2.5 degrees with 47 or 72 vertical layers up to 80 km, as COARDS-compliant NetCDF files ready for chemical transport and Earth system models, alongside NetCDF activity and rocket attribute files. It was produced at UCL and described in Scientific Data in 2024 under CC BY 4.0; the data are in the UCL Data Repository and the Python compilation scripts are on Zenodo. Caveats: only propellant type was known for eight vehicles, re-entry locations were mapped directly for 38% of the re-entry mass, and the period is three years. It supports environmental-impact and growth scenarios for space infrastructure; a related record is the UCL 2019 rocket emissions impact dataset.
